{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015y2cfpjejtm24cqebTvjsr","type":"tool_result","content":"=== bin/test.sh\n#!/bin/sh\n# CommandCenter Operation\n# Name: Test\n# Type: batch\n\n# Runs the csvstat verification gate: go vet, then go test, across the module.\nset -eu\n\nPROJECT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$PROJECT_DIR\"\n\ngo vet ./...\ngo test ./...\n=== cmd/csvstat/main.go\n// Command csvstat profiles one CSV file. Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Builds ./cmd/csvstat with `go build` and compares every command's exit code and standard output\n# over the supplied data files with the known answer below. Standard error is never compared.\n#\n#   sh sources/run.sh                    from the application root (how `drydock uat` runs it)\n#   sh uat/CsvStat/bin/run.sh APP        from anywhere, grading the application root APP\n#\n# Exit 0 only when the build succeeds and every check passes.\nset -u\n\nHERE=$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\nAPP=$(cd \"${1:-.}\" && pwd)\nif [ -f \"$HERE/employees.csv\" ]; then DATA=$HERE; else DATA=$(cd \"$HERE/../sources\" && pwd); fi\nWORK=$(mktemp -d)\ntrap 'rm -rf \"$WORK\"' EXIT INT TERM\nBIN=\"$WORK/csvstat\"\nMISSING=\"$WORK/no-such-file.csv\"\n\nif ! (cd \"$APP\" && go build -o \"$BIN\" ./cmd/csvstat); then\n    echo \"error: go build ./cmd/csvstat failed at the application root $APP.\" >&2\n    echo \"The deliverable is a Go module whose main package is ./cmd/csvstat.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nPASSED=0\nFAILED=0\n\n# check <id> <expected exit> <csvstat args...>  — expected standard output on stdin.\ncheck() {\n    id=$1\n    want_rc=$2\n    shift 2\n    cat > \"$WORK/want\"\n    (cd \"$APP\" && \"$BIN\" \"$@\") > \"$WORK/got\" 2> \"$WORK/err\"\n    rc=$?\n    if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want_rc\" ] && cmp -s \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\"; then\n        PASSED=$((PASSED + 1))\n        echo \"PASS $id: csvstat $*\"\n    else\n        FAILED=$((FAILED + 1))\n        echo \"FAIL $id: csvstat $*\"\n        echo \"  exit: expected $want_rc, got $rc\"\n        diff \"$WORK/want\" \"$WORK/got\" | sed 's/^/  /'\n        sed 's/^/  stderr: /' \"$WORK/err\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# ── A. One column ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\ncheck B1 0 --column salary \"$DATA/employees.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\nsalary,number,24,0,24,43699.25,147150.99,2085635.10,86901.46,79496.68\nEOF\ncheck B2 0 --column notes \"$DATA/employees.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\nnotes,text,24,10,4,mentor,\"remote, part-time\",,,\nEOF\ncheck B3 0 --column temp_c \"$DATA/sensors.csv\" <<'EOF'\ncolumn,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median\ntemp_c,number,36,3,32,-12.21,29.81,207.06,6.27,2.41\nEOF\n\n# ── C. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011XL4KqVZZDHzhf5a74c6SU","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t// Package cli parses the csvstat command line and dispatches it. Run takes its\n2\t// writers as arguments so tests drive it without touching the process streams.\n3\tpackage cli\n4\t\n5\timport (\n6\t\t\"errors\"\n7\t\t\"flag\"\n8\t\t\"fmt\"\n9\t\t\"io\"\n10\t)\n11\t\n12\t// Exit codes returned by Run. Only cmd/csvstat passes them to os.Exit.\n13\tconst (\n14\t\tExitOK          = 0 // success\n15\t\tExitOperational = 1 // the file cannot be opened or read\n16\t\tExitUsage       = 2 // invalid command line; checked before the file is opened\n17\t\tExitRejected    = 3 // rejected input: empty file, bad header, ragged record, unknown column\n18\t)\n19\t\n20\t// options holds the validated command line.\n21\ttype options struct {\n22\t\tfile   string\n23\t\tfreq   bool\n24\t\tcolumn string\n25\t\ttop    int\n26\t}\n27\t\n28\t// Run executes the csvstat command with args (excluding the program name) and\n29\t// returns the exit code. Help requests are written to help.\nfunc parse(args []string, help io.Writer) (options, error) {\n\tvar opts options\n\tfs := newFlagSet(&opts)\n\tif err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {\n\t\tif errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {\n\t\t\tfs.SetOutput(help)\n\t\t\tfs.Usage()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn options{}, err\n\t}\n\n\tset := make(map[string]bool)\n\tfs.Visit(func(f *flag.Flag) { set[f.Name] = true })\n\n\tif fs.NArg() != 1 {\n\t\treturn options{}, fmt.Errorf(\"expected exactly one FILE argument, got %d\", fs.NArg())\n\t}\n\topts.file = fs.Arg(0)\n\tif err := validate(opts, set); err != nil {\n\t\treturn options{}, err\n\t}\n\treturn opts, nil\n}\n\n// newFlagSet declares the options. Help requests are written to help.\nfunc parse(args []string, help io.Writer) (options, error) {\n\tvar opts options\n\tfs := newFlagSet(&opts)\n\tif err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {\n\t\tif errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {\n\t\t\tfs.SetOutput(help)\n\t\t\tfs.Usage()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn options{}, err\n\t}\n\n\tset := make(map[string]bool)\n\tfs.Visit(func(f *flag.Flag) { set[f.Name] = true })\n\n\tif fs.NArg() != 1 {\n\t\treturn options{}, fmt.Errorf(\"expected exactly one FILE argument, got %d\", fs.NArg())\n\t}\n\topts.file = fs.Arg(0)\n\tif err := validate(opts, set); err != nil {\n\t\treturn options{}, err\n\t}\n\treturn opts, nil\n}\n\n// newFlagSet declares the options. Its output is discarded so that parse errors\n// produce only the single diagnostic line written by Run.\nfunc newFlagSet(opts *options) *flag.FlagSet {\n\tfs := flag.NewFlagSet(\"csvstat\", flag.ContinueOnError)\n\tfs.SetOutput(io.Discard)\n\tfs.Usage = func() {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintln(fs.Output(), \"usage: csvstat [--column <name> | --freq <name> [--top <n>]] <file>\")\n\t\tfs.PrintDefaults()\n\t}\n\tfs.StringVar(&opts.freq, \"freq\", \"\", \"list the most frequent values of the named column\")\n\tfs.StringVar(&opts.column, \"column\", \"\", \"restrict output to the named column\")\n\tfs.IntVar(&opts.top, \"top\", defaultTop, \"number of frequent values to list (positive; requires --freq)\")\n\treturn fs\n}\n\n// validate applies the cross-option rules. set reports which flags were given\n// explicitly, so an unset --top is distinguishable from --top 0.\nfunc validate(opts options, set map[string]bool) error {\n\tif set[\"top\"] && !set[\"freq\"] {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"--top requires --freq\")\n\t}\n\tif set[\"top\"] && opts.top <= 0 {\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"--top must be a positive integer, got %d\", opts.top)\n\t}\n\tif set[\"freq\"] && set[\"column\"] {\n\t\treturn errors.New(\"--column cannot be used with --freq\")\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// profile reads and validates the file. cli\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\n// writeFile creates a file in a test-owned directory and returns its path.\nfunc writeFile(t *testing.T, content string) string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tpath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"input.csv\")\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"write fixture: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn path\n}\n\nfunc TestRunUsageErrors(t *testing.T) {\n\ttests := []struct {\n\t\tname string\n\t\targs []string\n\t}{\n\t\t{name: \"no arguments\", args: nil},\n\t\t{name: \"two files\", args: []string{\"a.csv\", \"b.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"unknown option\", args: []string{\"--bogus\", \"a.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"option missing value\", args: []string{\"--column\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"freq missing value\", args: []string{\"--freq\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"top zero with freq\", args: []string{\"--freq\", \"name\", \"--top\", \"0\", \"a.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"top negative with freq\", args: []string{\"--freq\", \"name\", \"--top=-1\", \"a.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"top not an integer\", args: []string{\"--freq\", \"name\", \"--top\", \"abc\", \"a.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"top without freq\", args: []string{\"--top\", \"3\", \"a.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"column with freq\", args: []string{\"--freq\", \"name\", \"--column\", \"x\", \"a.csv\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"freq without file\", args: []string{\"--freq\", \"name\"}},\n\t\t{name: \"option after file\", args: []string{\"a.csv\", \"--column\", \"x\"}},\n\t}\n\tfor _, tt := range {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01P7umBy749fsZ2Y889Uj4CM","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CsvStat/runs/20261025.001758/build/CsvStat/internal/csvdata/csvdata_test.go (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7497da99-91bc-4eea-b8d0-80e10e298e6c","uuid":"87521c44-b011-4eb2-be4a-779426f83041","timestamp":"2026-10-25T00:35:19.511Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"create","filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CsvStat/runs/20261025.001758/build/CsvStat/internal/csvdata/csvdata_test.go","content":"package csvdata\n\nimport (\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"io/fs\"\n\t\"os\"\n\t\"path/filepath\"\n\t\"reflect\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\n// writeFile creates a file in a test-owned directory and returns its path.\nfunc writeFile(t *testing.T, content string) string {\n\tt.Helper()\n\tpath := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"input.csv\")\n\tif err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(content), 0o600); err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"write fixture: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\treturn path\n}\n\nfunc mustRead(t *testing.T, path string) Table {\n\tt.Helper()\n\ttable, err := Read(path)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read(%s) error = %v\", path, err)\n\t}\n\treturn table\n}\n\nfunc TestReadTrimsHeaderAndValues(t *testing.T) {\n\tpath := writeFile(t, \" id , first name \\n 1 ,  Ada Lovelace  \\n   ,Grace\\n\")\n\ttable := mustRead(t, path)\n\n\twantHeader := []string{\"id\", \"first name\"}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(table.Header, wantHeader) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Header = %q, want %q\", table.Header, wantHeader)\n\t}\n\twantRecords := []Record{\n\t\t{Line: 2, Fields: []string{\"1\", \"Ada Lovelace\"}},\n\t\t{Line: 3, Fields: []string{\"\", \"Grace\"}},\n\t}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(table.Records, wantRecords) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Records = %+v, want %+v\", table.Records, wantRecords)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadQuotedFieldWithComma(t *testing.T) {\n\tpath := writeFile(t, \"id,notes\\n1,\\\"relocating to Austin, TX\\\"\\n2,\\\"say \\\"\\\"hi\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\")\n\ttable := mustRead(t, path)\n\n\twantRecords := []Record{\n\t\t{Line: 2, Fields: []string{\"1\", \"relocating to Austin, TX\"}},\n\t\t{Line: 3, Fields: []string{\"2\", `say \"hi\"`}},\n\t}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(table.Records, wantRecords) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Records = %+v, want %+v\", table.Records, wantRecords)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadReturnsRaggedRecordsWithLineNumbers(t *testing.T) {\n\tpath := writeFile(t, \"a,b,c\\n1,2,3\\n4,5\\n6,7,8,9\\n\")\n\ttable := mustRead(t, path)\n\n\tif len(table.Records) != 3 {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"len(Records) = %d, want 3\", len(table.Records))\n\t}\n\twantWidths := []int{3, 2, 4}\n\twantLines := []int{2, 3, 4}\n\tfor i, rec := range table.Records {\n\t\tif got := len(rec.Fields); got != wantWidths[i] {\n\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Records[%d] width = %d, want %d\", i, got, wantWidths[i])\n\t\t}\n\t\tif rec.Line != wantLines[i] {\n\t\t\tt.Errorf(\"Records[%d].Line = %d, want %d\", i, rec.Line, wantLines[i])\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadEmptyFileHasNoHeaderOrRecords(t *testing.T) {\n\ttable := mustRead(t, writeFile(t, \"\"))\n\tif len(table.Header) != 0 || len(table.Records) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Read(empty) = %+v, want no header and no records\", table)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadSyntaxErrorIsRejectedWithLine(t *testing.T) {\n\tpath := writeFile(t, \"a,b\\n1,2\\n3,x\\\"y\\n\")\n\t_, err := Read(path)\n\n\tvar reject *RejectError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &reject) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read(bare quote) error = %v, want *RejectError\", err)\n\t}\n\tif reject.Line != 3 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"RejectError.Line = %d, want 3\", reject.Line)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadMissingFileWrapsPathError(t *testing.T) {\n\t_, err := Read(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), \"absent.csv\"))\n\n\tvar pathErr *fs.PathError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &pathErr) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read(missing) error = %v, want *fs.PathError\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar reject *RejectError\n\tif errors.As(err, &reject) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Read(missing) error = %v, must not be a content rejection\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadDirectoryWrapsPathError(t *testing.T) {\n\t_, err := Read(t.TempDir())\n\n\tvar pathErr *fs.PathError\n\tif !errors.As(err, &pathErr) {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read(directory) error = %v, want *fs.PathError\", err)\n\t}\n\tvar reject *RejectError\n\tif errors.As(err, &reject) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Read(directory) error = %v, must not be a content rejection\", err)\n\t}\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01P7umBy749fsZ2Y889Uj4CM","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgN1zzNqAJS9XXmdx8AUb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01VHbqFBHCnjFYi6JANNApbW","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"mkdir -p /tmp/csvstat-check && cat > /tmp/csvstat-check/check.sh <<'EOF'\n#!/bin/sh\n# Checks block-2 acceptance cases against a built binary; prints one line per case.\nAPP=$1\nBIN=$2\nDATA=$APP/sources\nW=$(mktemp -d)\ncd \"$APP\" || exit 1\nfails=0\n# expect <want-exit> <label> <args...>  — also requires empty stdout\nexpect() {\n  want=$1; label=$2; shift 2\n  \"$BIN\" \"$@\" >\"$W/out\" 2>\"$W/err\"; rc=$?\n  n=$(wc -c <\"$W/out\" | tr -d ' ')\n  if [ \"$rc\" -eq \"$want\" ] && [ \"$n\" -eq 0 ]; then echo \"ok   $label (exit $rc)\"; else echo \"FAIL $label: exit $rc want $want, stdout bytes $n, stderr: $(cat \"$W/err\")\"; fails=$((fails+1)); fi\n}\nexpect_not2() {\n  label=$1; shift\n  \"$BIN\" \"$@\" >\"$W/out\" 2>\"$W/err\"; rc=$?\n  if [ \"$rc\" -ne 2 ]; then echo \"ok   $label (exit $rc)\"; else echo \"FAIL $label: usage error\";
